problems.explain: Try θ = 45°: tan(−45°) = −1, but tan 45° = 1. One angle where both sides are defined and differ disproves it. It does hold at 0° and 180°, so one angle tried there would mislead. (Tangent is odd: tan(−θ) = −tan θ.) So not always true.

prompt.v: Is tan θ cot θ = 1 true for every θ where both sides are defined?

problems.text: identity or not: tan(t)*cot(t) = 1
problems.explain: cot θ = 1/tan θ, and a number times its reciprocal is 1, so tan θ cot θ = 1 holds for every θ where both sides are defined: it is an identity. (Trying angles could only fail to find a counterexample; it is the derivation that shows it always holds.) So always true.
